quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The local orchestra usually performs in the town hall. However, this month's concert will be held in the botanical garden because the hall is being repaired. Tickets cost the same as always. The orchestra has about sixty musicians and was founded thirty years ago.
quests.question: The concert this month will take place in the town hall.
quests.hint: Look for where this month's concert will be held.
quests.explanation: The hall is under repair, so the concert moves to the botanical garden.
quests.evidenceLine: However, this month's concert will be held in the botanical garden because the hall is being repaired.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Pavel used to buy lunch at a café near his office every day. Now he only eats out on Fridays. The change began after he calculated how much he spent in a year and started bringing lunch from home.
quests.question: Pavel eats lunch out less often than he used to.
quests.hint: Compare his old routine with his new one.
quests.explanation: He used to eat out daily and now does so only on Fridays.
quests.evidenceLine: Pavel used to buy lunch at a café near his office every day. Now he only eats out on Fridays.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: A new food truck opened near the university last month. It sells burritos and salads, and students can order online to skip the line. On weekends, it moves to the main square. The owner, a former student, started the business with money she had saved.
quests.question: The food truck stays near the university on weekends.
quests.hint: Where does the truck go at the weekend?
quests.explanation: On weekends it moves to the main square.
quests.evidenceLine: On weekends, it moves to the main square.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Mariam's grandmother lives alone in a village two hours away. Mariam visits her every second weekend and calls her on the other evenings. Her cousin Yusuf lives closer, so he stops by each Sunday. Their phone calls usually last about half an hour and are full of family news.
quests.question: Yusuf visits the grandmother less often than Mariam does.
quests.hint: Compare how often each cousin visits.
quests.explanation: Yusuf visits every Sunday, while Mariam goes only every second weekend.
quests.evidenceLine: Mariam visits her every second weekend and calls her on the other evenings. Her cousin Yusuf lives closer, so he stops by each Sunday.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The company introduced flexible hours last year. Employees can start anywhere between 7 a.m. and 10 a.m., as long as they work eight hours. Many parents say it makes mornings easier. Managers report that the system has not lowered the quality of the work.
quests.question: Employees may start work as late as noon.
quests.hint: Find the latest allowed start time.
quests.explanation: The latest start is 10 a.m., not noon.
quests.evidenceLine: Employees can start anywhere between 7 a.m. and 10 a.m., as long as they work eight hours.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The documentary follows a family of fishermen for three years. The director spent months living in the village before starting to film, so that people would feel comfortable around the camera. Critics praise the film for its honest and natural scenes. The film was shown at several festivals and will be on television this winter.
quests.question: The director lived in the village first so people would feel at ease on camera.
quests.hint: Why did the director stay in the village?
quests.explanation: He lived there for months so the villagers would feel comfortable with the camera.
quests.evidenceLine: The director spent months living in the village before starting to film, so that people would feel comfortable around the camera.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Hikers who plan to climb the mountain should start before sunrise. The path is steep, and afternoon storms are common, so reaching the top by noon is safest. Water is not available along the route. A guide can be hired at the visitor center for an extra fee.
quests.question: Hikers need to carry their own water.
quests.hint: Read the third sentence about the route.
quests.explanation: No water is available on the route, so hikers must bring their own.
quests.evidenceLine: Water is not available along the route.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Crows are among the most intelligent birds. In one experiment, a crow bent a piece of wire into a hook to lift a small basket of food out of a tube. Scientists had not shown it how to do this. The result surprised the researchers, who repeated the test with several other birds.
quests.question: The scientists did not leave the crow to work out the hook alone.
quests.hint: Did anyone teach the crow?
quests.explanation: The passage says the scientists had not shown the crow how to do it.
quests.evidenceLine: Scientists had not shown it how to do this.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Zeynep's teacher gave the class a choice for the final project. Students could write a report of five pages or make a ten-minute presentation. Zeynep chose the presentation because she likes speaking in front of people. The final projects will be graded by two teachers in the last week of May.
quests.question: Zeynep picked the option that involved speaking.
quests.hint: Which option did Zeynep choose?
quests.explanation: She chose the presentation, and giving one means speaking to an audience.
quests.evidenceLine: Students could write a report of five pages or make a ten-minute presentation. Zeynep chose the presentation because she likes speaking in front of people.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: In many cities, people celebrate the New Year with fireworks at midnight. In Spain, people also eat twelve grapes, one with each chime of the clock. The tradition is said to bring good luck for the coming year. Some families prepare the grapes in small bowls ahead of time so nobody misses one.
quests.question: People in Spain eat twelve grapes for luck at New Year.
quests.hint: Look at the Spanish tradition and its purpose.
quests.explanation: Spanish people eat twelve grapes, and the custom is said to bring good luck.
quests.evidenceLine: In Spain, people also eat twelve grapes, one with each chime of the clock. The tradition is said to bring good luck for the coming year.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Adnan planned to paint his living room himself to save money. After two days of work, he realized that the walls needed more preparation than he had expected. In the end, he hired a professional painter to finish the job. He says the experience taught him which jobs are worth paying for.
quests.question: Adnan painted the entire room by himself.
quests.hint: Read how the project ended.
quests.explanation: He hired a professional to finish, so he did not do it all alone.
quests.evidenceLine: After two days of work, he realized that the walls needed more preparation than he had expected. In the end, he hired a professional painter to finish the job.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: A rainbow forms when sunlight passes through raindrops and splits into different colors. To see one, the sun must be behind you, and the rain must be in front of you. A rainbow is never seen when you face the sun. Double rainbows appear when light reflects twice inside the drops.
quests.question: You can see a rainbow when the sun is in front of you.
quests.hint: Where must the sun be for a rainbow to appear?
quests.explanation: The sun must be behind the viewer, not in front.
quests.evidenceLine: To see one, the sun must be behind you, and the rain must be in front of you.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Learners often think that a word-for-word translation is the best way to understand a new language. However, many idioms cannot be translated literally. For example, "it's raining cats and dogs" has nothing to do with animals. Good dictionaries therefore explain the meaning of common expressions instead of translating them.
quests.question: A literal translation of "raining cats and dogs" would explain what it really means.
quests.hint: Read what the passage says about idioms.
quests.explanation: The idiom has nothing to do with animals, so a literal translation would mislead.
quests.evidenceLine: However, many idioms cannot be translated literally. For example, "it's raining cats and dogs" has nothing to do with animals.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Mika has been learning to play the piano for six months. At first she practiced only ten minutes a day, but now she plays for half an hour. Her teacher says she has improved faster than most beginners. She hopes to perform a short piece at the school concert in June.
quests.question: Mika now practices three times as long as she did at first.
quests.hint: Compare ten minutes with half an hour.
quests.explanation: Thirty minutes is three times as long as ten minutes.
quests.evidenceLine: At first she practiced only ten minutes a day, but now she plays for half an hour.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: A community garden opened on the vacant lot next to the school. Neighbors grow vegetables there and share the harvest with a local food bank. Anyone can join, but new members must attend a short introduction. The food bank collects the vegetables every Friday afternoon.
quests.question: The garden is open to students of the school but closed to other neighbors.
quests.hint: Who is allowed to join?
quests.explanation: Anyone can join, not just students, after a short introduction.
quests.evidenceLine: Anyone can join, but new members must attend a short introduction.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Heat waves are becoming more frequent in many parts of the world. During a heat wave, doctors advise people to drink water regularly and stay in the shade at midday. Older adults and small children are most at risk. Cities are opening cool rooms in libraries so that people can rest during the hottest hours.
quests.question: Doctors say healthy adults are most at risk in a heat wave.
quests.hint: Who does the passage say is most at risk?
quests.explanation: Older adults and small children face the greatest risk.
quests.evidenceLine: Older adults and small children are most at risk.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Rafael put $200 into a savings account that pays 3 percent interest per year. After one year, he will have earned $6 in interest. He plans to leave the money there for five years. The bank sends him a short statement every three months.
quests.question: After one year, Rafael's savings will be worth $206.
quests.hint: Add the interest to the amount he deposited.
quests.explanation: $200 plus $6 in interest makes $206.
quests.evidenceLine: Rafael put $200 into a savings account that pays 3 percent interest per year. After one year, he will have earned $6 in interest.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Ling reads a few pages of a novel every night before bed. Some nights she is so tired that she only reads a paragraph. She has finished twelve books this year using this habit. Her sister recommended the habit after reading about it in a magazine.
quests.question: Ling does not read at all on nights when she feels tired.
quests.hint: Check Ling's routine on very tired nights.
quests.explanation: She still reads, though only a paragraph.
quests.evidenceLine: Some nights she is so tired that she only reads a paragraph.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Rice can be cooked in many ways, but the amount of water matters most. Long-grain rice usually needs about two cups of water for each cup of rice. Too much water makes it sticky, while too little leaves it hard. Most cooks also rinse the rice first to remove extra starch.
quests.question: Two cups of long-grain rice call for about four cups of water.
quests.hint: Use the ratio of water to rice.
quests.explanation: Each cup of rice needs about two cups of water, so two cups need four.
quests.evidenceLine: Long-grain rice usually needs about two cups of water for each cup of rice.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Most houseplants die from too much water rather than too little. Roots that stay wet all the time cannot get enough air and begin to rot. It is better to wait until the soil feels dry before watering again. Pots with drainage holes make the problem much less likely.
quests.question: Houseplants usually die because they are watered too rarely.
quests.hint: Look for the usual cause of death.
quests.explanation: The passage says overwatering, not too little water, is the usual cause.
quests.evidenceLine: Most houseplants die from too much water rather than too little.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: A new flu vaccine is needed each year because the virus changes quickly. Doctors update the vaccine to match the types that are expected to be most common. People over sixty-five are especially encouraged to get vaccinated. Pharmacies in many towns offer the shot without an appointment.
quests.question: The flu vaccine is updated because the virus keeps changing.
quests.hint: Find the reason for a yearly vaccine.
quests.explanation: The virus changes quickly, so a new vaccine is needed each year.
quests.evidenceLine: A new flu vaccine is needed each year because the virus changes quickly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Interns at Bright Media do not receive a salary, but they gain experience. After three months, the best interns are offered a paid contract. Last year, four out of ten interns were hired. The program runs twice a year, and applications close two months before it starts.
quests.question: Some interns are offered paid work after three months.
quests.hint: Read what is offered to the best interns.
quests.explanation: The best interns are offered a paid contract after three months.
quests.evidenceLine: After three months, the best interns are offered a paid contract.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Alvaro's tablet has two cameras: one on the front for video calls and one on the back for photos. He uses the front camera when he talks to his family. The back camera has a better lens. The tablet also has a small light next to the rear lens.
quests.question: Alvaro uses the back camera for video calls.
quests.hint: Which camera is used for calls?
quests.explanation: The front camera is for video calls, and Alvaro uses it to talk to his family.
quests.evidenceLine: Alvaro's tablet has two cameras: one on the front for video calls and one on the back for photos. He uses the front camera when he talks to his family.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The public library on Green Avenue has moved to a larger building. The new location is two blocks away and has a children's room and a quiet study area. It opens at 9 a.m. from Monday to Saturday. Residents can also return books through a slot in the door at any time of day.
quests.question: The library moved to a smaller building.
quests.hint: Look at how the new building is described.
quests.explanation: The library moved to a larger building, not a smaller one.
quests.evidenceLine: The public library on Green Avenue has moved to a larger building.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The city football team won only two of its first ten games this season. After a new coach took over, it won seven of the next ten. Fans now hope the team can qualify for the final tournament. The next match is against the team that is currently in first place.
quests.question: The team did better after the coach changed.
quests.hint: Compare the results before and after the new coach.
quests.explanation: It won two of ten before and seven of ten after the change.
quests.evidenceLine: The city football team won only two of its first ten games this season. After a new coach took over, it won seven of the next ten.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: When Tam opened his café, he offered only coffee and tea. Customers kept asking for food, so he added sandwiches and soups. Now the café is often full at lunchtime, and he is thinking of hiring a second cook.
quests.question: Tam added food because customers asked for it.
quests.hint: Why did Tam add sandwiches and soups?
quests.explanation: The passage says customers kept asking for food.
quests.evidenceLine: Customers kept asking for food, so he added sandwiches and soups.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Before refrigerators became common in homes, people preserved food with salt, smoke, or ice. Ice was cut from frozen lakes in winter and stored in special buildings. Some families received deliveries of ice throughout the summer. Ice was kept in wooden cabinets lined with metal so that it melted slowly.
quests.question: Before refrigerators, some households had ice delivered in summer.
quests.hint: Read the third sentence about summer.
quests.explanation: Some families received ice deliveries throughout the summer.
quests.evidenceLine: Some families received deliveries of ice throughout the summer.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Hiba's twins were born in March, so their birthday parties are always small and cozy. Because the weather in March is cold and rainy, the parties are held indoors. Last year, twelve children came to their apartment. Each child gets one small gift, and the family bakes a cake together.
quests.question: The twins' parties are usually held outdoors.
quests.hint: Where are the parties held, and why?
quests.explanation: Cold, rainy March weather means the parties take place indoors.
quests.evidenceLine: Because the weather in March is cold and rainy, the parties are held indoors.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: A streaming service is testing a feature that lets viewers skip a show's opening credits. The button appears after the first few seconds, and it is available for every episode. The company says the change is meant to make watching series easier. Some viewers have said they would still like a way to skip the recap.
quests.question: The new feature is designed to make viewing series easier.
quests.hint: Read what the company wants the change to do.
quests.explanation: The company says the change is meant to make watching series easier.
quests.evidenceLine: The company says the change is meant to make watching series easier.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Before using a ladder, check that it stands on a flat, dry surface. Never stand on the top step, because it is the easiest place to lose balance. A second person should hold the ladder if it is taller than three meters. Ladders with rubber feet are less likely to slip on smooth floors.
quests.question: Standing on the top step of a ladder is unsafe.
quests.hint: Read the second sentence about the top step.
quests.explanation: The passage says the top step is the easiest place to lose balance.
quests.evidenceLine: Never stand on the top step, because it is the easiest place to lose balance.
